## Introduction

Hazard pointers protect lock-free reclamation, but a single cell abstraction makes the common publish and retire pattern safer for concurrent data structures.

## Proposed Interface

```cpp
template<class T>
class hazard_cell {
public:
  T* protect() const noexcept;
  void retire(T* old) noexcept;
};
```

| Operation | Memory order | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| protect | acquire | no |
| retire | release | no |

## Wording

Insert into [saferecl.hp] a new paragraph:

> A `hazard_cell<T>` holds at most one protected pointer to an object of type `T` and defers its reclamation until no hazard pointer protects it.
